concept.concept_description: The cyclotomic matrix $A_k(\chi) = [G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})]$ involving Gauss sums over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ (where $N=p^m$ and $n=\varphi(N)/k$) can be decomposed as the matrix product $W D W^T$, where $W$ is the $n \times n$ discrete Fourier transform matrix with entries $W_{i,a} = \omega^{ai}$ ($\omega$ being a primitive $n$-th root of unity) and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of the $n$ Gauss periods $\eta_a$ corresponding to the $k$-th power residue cyclotomic cosets.
concept.mathematical_framing: The cyclotomic matrix $A_k(\chi) = [G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})]$ involving Gauss sums over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ (where $N=p^m$ and $n=\varphi(N)/k$) can be decomposed as the matrix product $W D W^T$, where $W$ is the $n \times n$ discrete Fourier transform matrix with entries $W_{i,a} = \omega^{ai}$ ($\omega$ being a primitive $n$-th root of unity) and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of the $n$ Gauss periods $\eta_a$ corresponding to the $k$-th power residue cyclotomic cosets.
concept.lean_guess: Rewrite the Gauss sum $G_N(\chi^{k(i+j)})$ by partitioning the summation over $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ into the $n$ cyclotomic cosets $C_a$ modulo $k$. Express $\chi^{k(i+j)}(x)$ as $\omega^{a(i+j)}$ for $x \in C_a$, pulling the root of unity out of the sum to yield $\sum_{a=0}^{n-1} \omega^{a(i+j)} \eta_a$, which directly translates to the matrix factorization $A_k(\chi) = W D W^T$.
